pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: It is non-depleting and does not cause cytokine release syndrome, unlike ATG. Main risks are hypersensitivity and infection.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: How does antithymocyte globulin (ATG) work?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: It is a polyclonal antibody preparation raised in animals against human T cells, which depletes circulating T lymphocytes to produce powerful immunosuppression.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: What are the main indications for antithymocyte globulin?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Induction immunosuppression in high immunological risk transplant, and treatment of acute steroid-resistant rejection. It is also used in aplastic anaemia.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: A transplant patient has biopsy-proven acute rejection that has not responded to steroids. What immunosuppressant can be used?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Antithymocyte globulin (ATG), a T-cell-depleting polyclonal antibody used for steroid-resistant acute rejection.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: What is the key acute toxicity of antithymocyte globulin, and how is it presented?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Cytokine release syndrome / first-dose reaction, presenting with fever, chills and hypotension. Prevent it by premedicating with steroid, antihistamine and paracetamol and infusing slowly.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: How is antithymocyte globulin administered to reduce first-dose reactions?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: As a slow IV infusion with premedication (steroid, antihistamine and paracetamol) and careful titration of the infusion rate.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: Why does antithymocyte globulin mandate CMV prophylaxis?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Its profound T-cell depletion greatly increases opportunistic infection risk, so valganciclovir prophylaxis is given to prevent CMV disease.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: Besides infections and cytokine release syndrome, what other complications can antithymocyte globulin cause?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), serum sickness, and cytopenias including thrombocytopenia.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: Contrast basiliximab and antithymocyte globulin for transplant induction.
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Basiliximab is a non-depleting anti-CD25 (IL-2 receptor) antibody for standard/low-risk induction and causes no cytokine release syndrome. ATG is T-cell-depleting, used for high-risk induction and steroid-resistant rejection, and can cause cytokine release syndrome.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: Which two immunosuppressants both work by blocking lymphocyte purine synthesis, and how do they differ in a key safety check?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Mycophenolate mofetil and azathioprine both block lymphocyte purine synthesis. Azathioprine requires TPMT testing before starting and has the dangerous allopurinol interaction; MMF is highly teratogenic and often replaces azathioprine.

pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.front: Why are live vaccines contraindicated in patients on these transplant immunosuppressants (MMF, azathioprine, basiliximab, ATG)?
pharmacology__Oncology & Immunosuppressi.back: Immunosuppression impairs the ability to control the attenuated organism, risking disseminated infection from the vaccine. Live vaccines should be avoided.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the main contraceptive mechanism of the combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP)?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: It mainly inhibits ovulation: the progestogen abolishes the LH surge and the oestrogen suppresses FSH. It also thickens cervical mucus and thins the endometrium.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Within the COCP, which component is the main ovulation suppressor and what does the oestrogen add?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The progestogen is the main ovulation suppressor (abolishes the LH surge). The oestrogen suppresses FSH, stabilises the endometrium (better cycle control) and potentiates the ovulation-suppressing effect.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Besides contraception, name several non-contraceptive benefits of the COCP.
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Regulates and lightens periods, helps acne, PMS and endometriosis, helps menstrual migraine without aura, and reduces the risk of ovarian and endometrial cancer.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman with migraine WITH aura asks to start the COCP. What do you advise and why?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The COCP is contraindicated (UKMEC 4) in migraine with aura because oestrogen further increases the ischaemic stroke risk. Offer a progestogen-only method instead.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: List the key UKMEC 4 (absolute) contraindications to the COCP.
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Migraine with aura, history of VTE or thrombophilia, age >35 and smoking >=15/day, BP >=160/100, current breast cancer, <6 weeks postpartum and breastfeeding, major surgery/immobility, and active liver disease.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Can a 37-year-old who smokes 20 cigarettes a day use the COCP?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: No. Age >35 combined with smoking >=15/day is UKMEC 4 (contraindicated) because of the increased cardiovascular/arterial risk. Offer a progestogen-only or non-hormonal method.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the most important serious risk of the COCP, and what symptoms should a woman report urgently?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Venous thromboembolism (VTE). She should urgently report calf pain/swelling or breathlessness/chest pain (DVT/PE), and sudden severe headache, focal weakness or visual/speech change (stroke/MI).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Which progestogens in the COCP carry a higher VTE risk, and how does that risk compare with pregnancy?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The third/fourth-generation progestogens (desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone) carry a higher VTE risk than levonorgestrel or norethisterone. However, the VTE risk on any COCP is still lower than the VTE risk in pregnancy.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Beyond VTE, what other cardiovascular and malignancy risks are linked to the COCP?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Increased ischaemic stroke and MI risk (especially in migraine-with-aura and smokers), hypertension, and a small increase in breast and cervical cancer risk that reverses after stopping.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How is the COCP conventionally taken?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: One pill daily for 21 days followed by a 7-day break (during which a withdrawal bleed occurs), or taken continuously/tailored. It should be taken every day at roughly the same time.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman on the COCP is booked for major abdominal surgery. What contraceptive advice do you give?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Stop the COCP 4 weeks before major or leg surgery or prolonged immobility, because of the increased VTE risk. Advise an alternative method and restart only when fully mobile.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What must you check before starting the COCP, and what BP reading means you should not start it?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Check BP and BMI before starting and at review. Do not start the COCP if BP is >=140/90.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman on the COCP is started on rifampicin (an enzyme inducer). How does this affect contraception and what should you do?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Enzyme inducers reduce COCP efficacy. Rather than just adding extra precautions, switch to an unaffected method (DMPA injection, IUS or copper IUD).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Name common enzyme-inducing drugs that reduce COCP efficacy.
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, some HIV drugs, and St John's Wort.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Why is the COCP problematic in a woman taking lamotrigine for epilepsy?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The COCP lowers lamotrigine levels, risking loss of seizure control. Also, stopping the COCP causes lamotrigine levels to rise again, risking lamotrigine toxicity.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the main contraceptive mechanism of the progestogen-only pill (POP)?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Progestogen alone: the traditional POP mainly thickens cervical mucus, while the desogestrel POP also inhibits ovulation. Both thin the endometrium.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Why is the POP suitable when the COCP is contraindicated?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The POP contains no oestrogen, so it carries no VTE or stroke risk. It can therefore be used in women with VTE history, migraine with aura, breastfeeding women, smokers over 35, and those with hypertension.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A breastfeeding woman needs contraception but has migraine with aura. Is the POP appropriate?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Yes. The POP is oestrogen-free (no VTE/stroke risk) and is suitable in both breastfeeding and migraine with aura, where the COCP is contraindicated.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How is the POP taken compared with the COCP?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The POP is taken every single day with no break (no pill-free week), at the same time each day.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the missed-pill window for a traditional POP versus a desogestrel POP?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The traditional POP has a strict 3-hour window; the desogestrel POP has a 12-hour window. A pill taken later than this counts as missed and needs backup (e.g. condoms).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the commonest side effect and reason for discontinuing the POP?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Irregular, unpredictable bleeding is the main side effect and the commonest reason women stop the POP. Other effects include acne, breast tenderness and a small ovarian-cyst risk.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman on the POP needs to start carbamazepine. What contraceptive change is advised?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Enzyme inducers reduce POP efficacy, and the POP is not recommended with inducers. Switch to an unaffected method such as DMPA, IUS or copper IUD.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is a key absolute contraindication to the POP?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Current breast cancer. Use caution with undiagnosed vaginal bleeding and active liver disease.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What are the three options for emergency contraception and their time limits?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Levonorgestrel within 72 hours, ulipristal within 120 hours, and the copper IUD within 5 days (the most effective option).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Which emergency contraceptive method is the most effective, and how does it work?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The copper IUD is the most effective (up to 5 days after unprotected sex). It works primarily by preventing implantation, so it is effective even after ovulation.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How do oral levonorgestrel and ulipristal work as emergency contraception?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Both delay ovulation; neither disrupts an established pregnancy. They are ineffective once the LH surge has begun, though ulipristal (a progesterone-receptor modulator) can still delay an already-rising surge, so works closer to ovulation and is more effective.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Why is ulipristal considered more effective than levonorgestrel for emergency contraception?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Levonorgestrel only works before the LH surge, whereas ulipristal (an SPRM) can still delay an already-rising LH surge. Ulipristal therefore works closer to ovulation.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the dose of emergency levonorgestrel, and when is it doubled?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg stat, doubled to 3 mg if weight >70 kg or BMI >26.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the dose of ulipristal for emergency contraception, and is it dose-adjusted for weight?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Ulipristal 30 mg stat. It is not dose-doubled for higher weight/BMI.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman on an enzyme inducer needs emergency contraception. What is preferred?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The copper IUD is preferred. If oral is used, off-label double-dose (3 mg) levonorgestrel is the fallback; ulipristal should be avoided with enzyme inducers.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Why should ulipristal be avoided if a progestogen was taken recently?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Ulipristal and progestogens interfere mutually. Avoid ulipristal if a progestogen was taken in the prior 7 days, as it reduces ulipristal's effectiveness.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: After giving ulipristal, when can hormonal contraception be started?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Wait 5 days after ulipristal before starting or restarting hormonal contraception (because they interfere mutually), using condoms in the meantime.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman vomits 90 minutes after taking her emergency contraceptive pill. What should you do?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Repeat the dose, because vomiting within 2-3 hours means it may not have been absorbed.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What caution applies to ulipristal in a woman with asthma?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Ulipristal should be used with caution in severe asthma that is inadequately controlled by oral steroids.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the breastfeeding advice after emergency contraception with ulipristal versus levonorgestrel?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: After ulipristal, express and discard breast milk for 1 week. Levonorgestrel is compatible with breastfeeding.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How does the levonorgestrel intrauterine system (LNG-IUS, e.g. Mirena/Kyleena) work as a contraceptive?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: It releases levonorgestrel locally in the uterus -> thins the endometrium and thickens cervical mucus (with some ovulation suppression) -> a very effective long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How long is the Mirena LNG-IUS now licensed for contraception, and the Kyleena?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Mirena is now licensed for 8 years; Kyleena for 5 years.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman with heavy menstrual bleeding wants an effective treatment that is also contraceptive. What is first-line?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The levonorgestrel intrauterine system (LNG-IUS, e.g. Mirena). It is first-line for heavy menstrual bleeding because local levonorgestrel thins the endometrium, making periods lighter or absent.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Besides contraception and heavy menstrual bleeding, name two other uses of the LNG-IUS.
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Endometrial protection when a woman is on HRT/oestrogen, and management of dysmenorrhoea/endometriosis.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What bleeding pattern should you warn a woman to expect after fitting an LNG-IUS?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Irregular bleeding/spotting in the first few months, then usually much lighter periods or no periods (amenorrhoea).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: List the contraindications to fitting an LNG-IUS.
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Current pelvic infection, unexplained vaginal bleeding, endometrial or cervical cancer, and a distorted uterine cavity.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What are the main insertion-related risks when fitting an intrauterine device (LNG-IUS or copper)?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Uterine perforation (higher if breastfeeding or <36 weeks postpartum), expulsion, and — if the device fails and pregnancy occurs — ectopic pregnancy.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman taking rifampicin (an enzyme inducer) needs reliable contraception. Why is the LNG-IUS a good choice?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Its action is local within the uterus, so it is unaffected by enzyme inducers (UKMEC 1). It is a first-choice alternative when enzyme inducers are being used.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What must be done before fitting any intrauterine device, and why?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Screen for and treat sexually transmitted infections before fitting, because insertion in the presence of infection risks pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: If an LNG-IUS is fitted at age 45 or over, how long can it be retained?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: It can be retained until menopause.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How does the copper IUD prevent pregnancy?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Copper is toxic to sperm and ova and creates a sterile inflammatory reaction in the endometrium -> it primarily prevents fertilisation. Inhibition of implantation is a back-up mechanism. It is non-hormonal.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How long does a copper IUD last, and when does it become effective?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: It is effective immediately and lasts 5-10 years (larger >=300 mm2 devices last 10 years; retain to menopause if fitted at >=40).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman presents 3 days after unprotected sex wanting the most effective emergency contraception. What do you offer?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The copper IUD — the most effective emergency contraception. It can be inserted up to 5 days after unprotected sex (or after expected ovulation).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the main downside of the copper IUD that you must counsel a woman about?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: It tends to cause heavier, longer and more painful periods (it is non-hormonal, so there is no progestogenic lightening of bleeding).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: List the contraindications to a copper IUD.
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Current pelvic infection, unexplained vaginal bleeding, distorted uterine cavity, Wilson's disease, and copper allergy.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Why is the copper IUD contraindicated in Wilson's disease?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Wilson's disease is a disorder of copper handling/accumulation, so a copper-releasing device is contraindicated.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Is the copper IUD affected by enzyme inducers such as rifampicin or carbamazepine?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: No. It is non-hormonal and acts locally, so it is unaffected by enzyme inducers (UKMEC 1).

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How does the depot progestogen injection (DMPA/Depo-Provera) work, and how often is it given?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate is a long-acting injected progestogen that inhibits ovulation (plus cervical mucus and endometrial effects) for about 13 weeks. It is given IM or SC every 12-13 weeks.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman finds daily pill-taking difficult. Why might the depot progestogen injection suit her?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: It is given only every 12-13 weeks, so it is useful when adherence is difficult, and it also reduces bleeding and period pain.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What are the distinctive side effects of the depot progestogen injection (DMPA) that set it apart from other progestogen methods?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Weight gain, a reversible reduction in bone mineral density, and a delayed return of fertility (up to about 1 year after stopping). Bleeding is initially irregular then usually amenorrhoea.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What happens to bone mineral density with DMPA, and how does this affect follow-up?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: DMPA causes a reversible reduction in bone mineral density that recovers on stopping. Reassess the risk/benefit if it is continued beyond 2 years. It is UKMEC 2 in women aged under 18 and over 45.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman stopping DMPA to conceive asks how quickly her fertility will return. What do you tell her?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: There can be a delayed return of fertility — it may take up to about 1 year after the last injection before fertility returns.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the contraindication to the depot progestogen injection (DMPA)?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Current breast cancer. Caution is also needed with osteoporosis risk factors, and it is UKMEC 2 at age <18 and >45 owing to the bone density concern.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Is the depot progestogen injection (DMPA) reduced by enzyme inducers?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: No. Depot progestogen levels are high, so it is not reduced by enzyme inducers, making it a recommended option when inducers preclude the COCP, POP or implant.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How does the progestogen implant (Nexplanon/etonogestrel) work, and how long does it last?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: A subdermal rod releases etonogestrel (a progestogen) that inhibits ovulation (plus mucus/endometrial effects). It lasts 3 years and is inserted subdermally in the upper arm.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Which reversible contraceptive is the most effective, and roughly what is its failure rate?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The progestogen implant (Nexplanon). It is a 'fit and forget' LARC with a failure rate of less than 1 in 1000.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the commonest reason women have the progestogen implant removed, and how should you counsel about it?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Unpredictable/irregular bleeding is the main issue and the commonest reason for removal. Counsel women about this before insertion so it is expected.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman on the progestogen implant is started on carbamazepine (an enzyme inducer). What should be done?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Enzyme inducers reduce the implant's efficacy, so switch her to a method unaffected by inducers — DMPA, copper IUD or LNG-IUS — rather than just adding an extra method.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What MHRA safety advice applies to inserting and removing the progestogen implant (Nexplanon)?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Palpate and document the implant's location after insertion. If it is impalpable, image it (ultrasound or X-ray) before attempting removal, because of rare deep or vascular migration.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: What is the contraindication to the progestogen implant?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Current breast cancer. In addition, enzyme inducers reduce its efficacy, so an alternative method should be used if these are needed.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: How do the LNG-IUS and the copper IUD differ in their effect on periods?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The LNG-IUS makes periods lighter or absent (local levonorgestrel thins the endometrium). The copper IUD is non-hormonal and tends to make periods heavier, longer and more painful.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: Which LARC methods are unaffected by enzyme inducers, and which contraceptives are affected?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: Unaffected: LNG-IUS and copper IUD (local action) and the depot progestogen injection (DMPA, high depot levels). Affected (efficacy reduced): the COCP, POP and progestogen implant.

pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.front: A woman needs contraception but has a distorted uterine cavity, so an intrauterine device cannot be fitted. Which non-oral, enzyme-inducer-proof options remain?
pharmacology__Obstetrics, Gynaecology &.back: The depot progestogen injection (DMPA) is unaffected by enzyme inducers. The progestogen implant is an option too, but its efficacy is reduced by enzyme inducers, so DMPA is preferred if inducers are involved.
